newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Bombardier gets US$600 million Regional Jet order.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bombardier gets US$600 million Regional Jet order.

text.p: Shares of Bombardier Inc rose sharply on the Toronto Stock Exchange Tuesday after Atlantic Southeast Airlines (ASA) said it had agreed to order 30 of its Canadair Regional Jet aircraft.
The US$600 million order is the single largest transaction for the 50-seat passenger jet.
ASA also agreed to options to purchase an additional 60 Regional Jet planes.
By early afternoon, Bombardier's shares were up 0.95 on the TSE to a new 52-week high of 26.35 on a brisk volume of more than one million shares.
Analysts said the order is a significant boost for Bombardier's Regional Jet program.
Before the ASA agreement, there were 176 Regional Jets on order, of which 142 were in service with 14 operators in eight countries, Bombardier said.
ASA is the fourth regional carrier in the United States to choose the Regional Jet, Bombardier said. Other commercial airline customers include Lufthansa's CityLine unit and Air Canada.
An analyst who declined to be identified said the ASA order places Bombardier at the forefront of developing international markets for its 50-seat and proposed 70-seat Regional Jet.

"It's a huge step forward in terms of what regional airlines have decided they will be flying into the next century," the analyst said. "I think that with this order Bombardier is sort of untouchable."
"It is monumental. That is how we view it. It confirms our production plans for the next year," Catherine Chase, spokeswoman for Bombardier's Canadair division, told Reuters.
Last year, Bombardier increased production of the Regional Jet to five a month from four.
There is speculation that, aside from ASA which is a Delta Connection carrier, other airlines contemplating the Regional Jet include American Eagle and Washington-based Atlantic Coast.
The ASA transaction also bodes well for the development of Bombardier's 70-seat CRJ-X jet.

In an announcement, ASA president John Beiser said the airline chose the Regional Jet because of its comfortable, four-abreast, quiet cabin and demonstrated reliability and economics. Beiser said ASA was also interested in Bombardier's development of the CRJ-X.
"The future availability of the 70-passenger CRJ-X ensures our airline will be strategically well-positioned for the future," he said.
Bombardier is seeking orders for the CRJ-X, but it's board of directors has not yet given final approval to production of the aircraft, which is a stretch version of the Regional Jet.

Bombardier's Chase declined to comment on other potential customers for the Regional Jet, but said the company already held 45 percent of the global market for 30-to-70-seat turboprop or jet passenger aircraft.
"We created the market and the acceptance (of the jet) is there by passengers and airlines in Europe, Asia and the United States," she said.

Last year, Bombardier was awarded a controversial C$87 million ($42 million) loan guarantee by the Canadian government to proceed with development of the CRJ-X. Bombardier had purchased Canadair, maker of the Regional Jet, in the early 1980s after Canadian taxpayers had poured roughly C$1 billion ($740 million) into the then struggling Challenger business jet manufacturer.

Since then, Bombardier has expanded its reach internationally and profitably in the aerospace sector, producing the Regional Jet, purchasing Ireland's Short Brothers and turning it around, and buying turboprop plane maker de Havilland, of Toronto, from Boeing Co.. Bombardier also owns Learjet Inc.

Bombardier has C$7 billion ($5.2 billion) of annual sales. It makes motorized consumer products like snowmobiles and personal watercraft, and rail transportation equipment, including the shuttle-train cars for the English Channel tunnel.
